cta_label.description: Button label, or empty when there is no button

description.description: Supporting copy, or empty
description.example: Complete verification to withdraw your earnings.

icon_url.description: The URL of the action's illustration icon, or null if it has none

status.description: required (act now) or pending (under review)

amount.description: Total held in this currency, in native units, as a decimal string. `usd` and `usdt` are reported as one `usd` entry, matching how the balance row groups them.

items.description: The total split by why each part is held. Only reasons holding a non-zero amount appear, so these can sum to less than `amount`, never more.

currency.description: Lowercase ISO currency code, such as `usd` or `eur`.

items.description: When the held money unlocks, one entry per day, earliest first. Money whose release depends on something other than a date is left out, so these can sum to less than `amount`, never more.

hold_period_days.description: Number of days reserved funds are held before release.

percentage.description: Percentage of incoming payment volume held in reserve. `null` when no reserve is applied.

amount.description: Amount held for this reason, in native units, as a decimal string.

hold_period_days.description: Days money is currently held for this reason before it unlocks, or `null` when release depends on something other than time. Money already held keeps the terms it was taken under.

percentage.description: Percentage of each incoming payment currently held for this reason, or `null` when the reason is not a percentage of anything. Money already held keeps the release date it was given, which `unlocks_by_date` reflects.

value.description: Choice text shown to the person.

keyword.description: Suggested reply the person can tap to start the conversation.

message.description: Greeting shown when the conversation opens.
message.example: Hi! Tell us your vehicle and ZIP and we will send an interior deep clean quote.

message.description: A description of what the issue is and how it can be resolved.
message.example: Your ad was rejected for unacceptable business practices. Edit the ad's content and resubmit.

resource_id.description: The ID of the campaign, ad group, or ad the issue is attached to.

resource_type.description: The type of resource the issue is attached to.

api_version_date.description: Dated API version used when requests authenticated with this key omit the `Api-Version-Date` header.

created_at.description: When the API key was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

expires_at.description: When the API key stops working, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` means it never expires.

items.description: The key's effective permissions, grouped by resource. Present on retrieve, create, update, and rotate responses; omitted on list.
IPv4/IPv6 CIDR ranges allowed to use this key. `null` or empty means requests are accepted from any IP.

is_default_for_resource.description: Whether this is the resource's default API key. Default keys cannot be updated or deleted, only rotated.

name.description: Human-readable name identifying the API key, or `null` when none was set.

obfuscated_secret_key.description: Masked version of the secret key, so the key can be recognized without revealing the full secret.

secret_key.description: The full secret used to authenticate requests. Returned only once, on create and rotate responses — store it immediately.

system_role.description: System role the key inherits its permissions from, or `null` when it uses an explicit permissions policy. Only account API keys can use a system role.

updated_at.description: When the API key was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

items.description: The actions the grant covers on the resource, each marked granted or not.

resource_id.description: ID of the resource the actions apply to.

resource_type.description: The type of resource the actions apply to, such as `account`, `product`, or `app`.

action.description: The permission action's identifier, for example `company:basic:read`.

granted.description: Whether the key holds the action on the grant's resource.

account.description: The account that owns the app.

api_key.description: Legacy app API key used to authenticate requests on the app's behalf. `null` when no key exists or the caller lacks the `developer:manage_api_key` permission.

app_store_description.description: Detailed description shown on the app store's in-depth app page, or `null` when none has been set.
app_store_description.example: Shine Time Booking turns a whop into a booking calendar. Members pick a package, choose a slot that fits the day's route, and pay up front. A reminder goes out the night before and the receipt lands as soon as the job is signed off.

app_type.description: The type of end-user the app is built for.

banner_image.description: Banner image from the app's product listing, or `null` when none is uploaded.

base_url.description: The production base URL where the app is hosted. `null` if no base URL is configured, if the caller lacks the `developer:basic:read` permission on the app's account, or on list responses, which never expose it.

items.description: Up to three logo image URLs from businesses created from this app as a template.

creator.description: The user who owns the publishing account.

dashboard_path.description: URL path for the account dashboard view, or `null` when not configured.

default_api_key.description: The app's default API key. `null` when the app has no default key or the caller lacks the `developer:manage_api_key` permission; `secret_key` is additionally `null` unless the caller could have created the key themselves.

deployment.description: What the app has left to publish, and how a publish in flight is going — `status` is only ever `unpublished`, `publishing`, or `failed` here. `null` means there is nothing to report: the app is fully published, there is no working copy to publish from, or the caller cannot deploy this app. Tell those apart from the app's own `production_web_build`.

discover_path.description: URL path for the discover view, or `null` when not configured.

domain_id.description: Subdomain identifier for the app's proxied URL, forming https://{domain_id}.apps.whop.com.

experience_path.description: URL path for the member-facing hub view, or `null` when not configured.

hosted_url.description: Full URL where the app's hosted web build is served, or `null` if no route is claimed.

icon.description: The app's icon. Falls back to the default app icon when none is uploaded.

marketplace_status.description: Approval status of the app's product listing on the Whop app store, or `null` when the app has no associated product.

name.description: Display name shown on the app store and in experience navigation.

oauth_client_type.description: How the app authenticates at the OAuth token endpoint.

openapi_path.description: URL path to the app's OpenAPI spec file, or `null` when not configured.

origin.description: Full origin URL of the app's proxied domain, for example https://ab1c2d3e4f.apps.whop.com.

product_id.description: ID of the app's product listing on the Whop app store, or `null` when the app has no associated product.

production_android_build.description: The approved build currently served on Android, or `null` when none is deployed.

production_ios_build.description: The approved build currently served on iOS, or `null` when none is deployed.

production_web_build.description: The approved build currently served on web, or `null` when none is deployed.

items.description: Whitelisted OAuth callback URLs users are redirected to after authorizing the app.

route.description: Claimed subdomain route where hosted web builds are served (`myapp` for myapp.whop.app), or `null` if no route is claimed.

secrets.description: The app's production secrets as an object of string values, injected into the hosted server runtime. `null` when the caller lacks the `developer:update_app` permission.

skills_path.description: URL path to the app's skills directory, or `null` when not configured.

platform.description: The target platform for this build.

review_message.description: Feedback from the reviewer explaining a rejection, or `null` if the build has not been reviewed or was approved.

source_url.description: URL to download the compressed source code archive that produced this build, or `null` when the build was uploaded without a source archive.

status.description: The build's review status.

items.description: The view types this build supports, as declared by the developer.

draft.description: Whether the running or last deployment uploaded a build without making it live.

estimated_duration_ms.description: How long this deployment is expected to take in total, estimated from previous runs.

estimated_remaining_ms.description: How much longer the deployment is expected to take. Held above zero until it actually finishes.

finished_at.description: When the deployment ended, in milliseconds since the epoch, or `null` while it is still running.

started_at.description: When the deployment began, in milliseconds since the epoch, or `null` when none has run.

justification.description: The developer's explanation of why the app needs the permission, or `null` when none was provided.
justification.example: Creates apps on behalf of the installing company.

permission_action.description: The permission action the app requests.

audience_type.description: `custom` = a customer list (uploaded, or built from saved People filters); `lookalike` = Meta lookalike built from a custom audience.

auto_refresh.description: Whether membership keeps updating. `true` rebuilds it from the saved filters twice a day, so people join and leave as they start and stop matching. `false` keeps whoever matched when it was built and never rebuilds. Always `false` for uploaded lists and lookalikes.

created_at.description: When the audience was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

error_message.description: Processing error message. `null` unless processing is partial or failed.
error_message.example: 412 of 1,000 rows had no email or phone number, so the list could not be matched.

filters.description: For audiences built from People filters: the filters that define membership, keyed exactly as `GET /people` accepts them — for example `{"os": "iOS", "country": "US"}`. `null` for uploaded lists and lookalikes.

last_refreshed_at.description: When the audience membership was last rebuilt, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` until the first build completes.

lookalike_ratio.description: For lookalikes: the upper bound of the similarity band as a fraction (0.02 = top 2%). `null` for custom audiences.

lookalike_starting_ratio.description: For lookalikes: the lower bound of the similarity band as a fraction. `null` for custom audiences and first-tier lookalikes.

items.description: Estimated match rates by ad platform. Empty when the audience was not sent to a supported platform.

matched_rows.description: Members successfully uploaded to connected ad accounts. Always 0 for lookalikes.

items.description: External audience IDs created on connected ad platforms, such as Meta.

processed_rows.description: Members processed from the source so far. Always 0 for lookalikes.

source_audience_id.description: For lookalikes: the audience this lookalike was built from. `null` for custom audiences.

source_type.description: Where members come from. `csv_upload` = an uploaded customer list; `people_filter` = built from saved People filters. See `auto_refresh` for whether a `people_filter` audience keeps updating.

status.description: Current state of the audience import. `syncing` means Whop is sending matched rows to connected ad accounts. When status is `partial` or `failed`, `error_message` explains what went wrong.

total_rows.description: Total members detected in the source — CSV rows for uploaded lists, matching people for automatic audiences. Always 0 for lookalikes.

updated_at.description: When the audience was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

lower_bound.description: Lower bound of the estimated match rate percentage. `null` until available.

platform.description: The ad platform that provided the match-rate estimate.

status.description: Availability of the estimated match rate.

upper_bound.description: Upper bound of the estimated match rate percentage. `null` until available.

items.description: The deliverable shapes this bounty accepts. Every bounty accepts any combination of `content_url` (posted links) and `media` (uploaded files), except `data_capture` bounties, whose proof is clips recorded in the Whop app that accumulate on the attempt.

accepted_submissions_limit.description: Number of submissions that can be accepted (winner slots).

accepted_submissions_per_user_limit.description: How many winner slots one worker can win. Defaults to `1`. Wins plus proofs awaiting review never exceed this number, and a worker runs one attempt at a time. Cannot exceed `accepted_submissions_limit`.

items.description: Proof livestreams live on this bounty right now, newest first — workers streaming their attempts. Empty when nothing is live.

affiliate_share_amount.description: What a referrer earns per accepted submission when the worker arrived through their affiliate link, in whole currency units, at the standard platform fee rate. Taken out of the worker's post-fee reward rather than added on top. `0` when the bounty pays no affiliate share, including bounties tied to no account, which cannot record a referral.

items.description: Countries whose residents can work the bounty, as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes. Empty means worldwide.

awaiting_review_submissions_count.description: Submissions delivered and waiting on review. A subset of `unresolved_submissions_count`, which also counts attempts still in progress.

budget_amount.description: Total gross budget committed to the bounty: `gross_reward_amount` times `accepted_submissions_limit`.

business_goal_type.description: What the poster wants the work to achieve, declared once at create. `null` for bounties created before the taxonomy rolled out.

cancel_requested_at.description: When cancellation was requested, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. On a `closed` bounty this means the cancel is pending: submissions are stopped and the bounty cancels once in-flight submissions resolve. On a `canceled` bounty it records when the cancellation was requested. `null` when no cancellation was ever requested.

capture_spec.description: The technical contract footage must be recorded against. Present only on `data_capture` bounties; `null` for every other goal type.

created_at.description: When the bounty was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Currency for all amounts on the bounty, as a lowercase ISO 4217 code.

description.description: Full task instructions shown to workers.
description.example: Record one continuous pass of a full interior detail, dash to trunk, on a customer vehicle.

discussion_experience_id.description: Experience the bounty's discussion thread lives in, prefixed `exp_`. Read this — not `experience_id` — to open the thread: a platform-wide bounty has no hosting experience of its own but its discussion still lives in one.

discussion_feed_id.description: Forum feed containing the bounty's discussion thread. `null` for a bounty with no forum post.

discussion_post_id.description: Forum post anchoring the bounty's discussion thread. Read together with `discussion_experience_id` to address the thread. `null` for a bounty with no forum post.

experience_id.description: Experience the bounty is hosted in, prefixed `exp_`. `null` for platform-wide bounties; may belong to a different account than the funder.

funding_account.description: Account whose balance funds the bounty pool, or `null` when a user funds it personally. May differ from the account hosting `experience_id`.

gross_paid_out_amount.description: Gross amount paid out from the bounty pool across accepted submissions — worker payouts, platform fees, and affiliate shares together. Tips and reviewer rewards are excluded.

gross_reward_amount.description: Gross bounty-pool amount allocated per accepted submission, in whole currency units.

hosting_account.description: Account hosting the bounty's forum — the one whose `route` and `experience_id` address its discussion thread, and where its submissions dashboard lives. `null` for a platform-wide bounty with no host. May differ from `funding_account`.

net_reward_amount.description: What a worker is quoted per accepted submission after the platform fee, in whole currency units. The exact post-fee figure, at the standard platform fee rate — a worker who locked a different rate, or who arrived through an affiliate link, is paid a different amount.

poster.description: User who posted the bounty — the account owner when created with an account API key.

scheduled_frequency.description: How often the schedule creates a new bounty. Each occurrence is a separate bounty; the original is not republished.

scheduled_publish_at.description: When a scheduled bounty will publish, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` once published, for bounties that were never scheduled, and for terminally failed drafts parked for manual rescheduling.

spots_remaining.description: Unfilled winner capacity: `accepted_submissions_limit` minus `accepted_submissions_count`, clamped to zero. Not on its own a signal that the bounty accepts new claims — read `status` for that: only an `open` bounty takes new submissions.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `scheduled` bounties are unpublished drafts, visible to their poster and the account's authorized managers; `open` bounties accept new submissions; `closed` bounties are live but no longer accept new submissions; `completed` bounties paid out every winner slot; `canceled` bounties ended before filling their slots.

submissions_closed_at.description: When new submissions stopped being accepted, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Set when a cancellation is requested on a bounty with work in flight, so in-flight submissions can resolve before the bounty cancels. `null` when submissions were never stopped — including completed bounties that simply filled every winner slot.

title.description: Short name of the task shown to workers.

unresolved_submissions_count.description: Submissions still awaiting an outcome: in progress or pending review.

updated_at.description: When the bounty was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

viewer_accepted_submissions_count.description: How many winner slots the authenticated user has already won on this bounty. Read against `accepted_submissions_per_user_limit` to show a worker their remaining allowance. `0` when the request has no authenticated user.

host.description: User hosting the proof livestream — the worker streaming their attempt. `null` if the host account no longer exists.

title.description: Display title for the proof livestream.

bounty_submission_id.description: The bounty submission (attempt) this clip belongs to, prefixed `btys_`.

created_at.description: When the clip was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

duration_seconds.description: Server-validated clip duration in whole seconds. `null` until validation completes.

failure_code.description: Stable validation failure code. `null` unless `status` is `failed`.

failure_message.description: Human-readable validation failure reason. `null` unless `status` is `failed`.
failure_message.example: video: The video upload failed after 5 retries.

frames_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the video frame timestamp log. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

imu_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope) log. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

manifest_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the capture manifest. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

ready_at.description: When server-side validation completed successfully, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` until then.

sequence.description: The clip's stable order within the attempt, starting at 1.

status.description: Recording and validation state. `recording` is still capturing; `verifying` is running server-side validation; `ready` passed validation and counts toward the verified-duration payout gate; `failed` did not validate.

updated_at.description: When the clip was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

video_url.description: Temporary signed URL for the synchronized MP4 video. Returned only on single-clip reads for an authorized viewer; `null` on list responses or until the artifact is attached.

captured_duration_seconds.description: Total verified duration of accepted capture clips, in whole seconds. `0` for submissions whose deliverable doesn't accumulate clips.

city.description: Capture metadata: city the footage was recorded in. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

claimed_at.description: When the worker claimed the submission, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

content.description: Written proof the worker submitted with their work.
content.example: Ceramic coating reveal, shot at the Burnet Rd bay

country.description: Capture metadata: country the footage was recorded in. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

created_at.description: When the submission was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

deliverable_type.description: How the work arrived when it came in through the API in one shot, informational only — read the work from `deliverable_urls`, `files`, and `capture_clips` directly. `null` for submissions whose proof is a livestream recording, including ones that attached links or files on submit.

items.description: Links submitted as work, followed by temporary download URLs for the uploaded files. `null` when the submission carries neither.

denial_reason.description: Why the submission was denied, when a presentable reason exists. Always `null` unless `status` is `denied`.

device.description: Capture metadata: device the footage was recorded on. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

items.description: Files uploaded as part of the work, in upload order. Empty when the submission has none.

fov.description: Capture metadata: horizontal field of view in degrees. `null` when not reported.

latest_proof_livestream_feed.description: Latest public proof livestream attached to the submission.

operator.description: Capture metadata: identifier of the person who recorded the footage. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

resolved_at.description: When the submission was approved or denied, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` until then.

site.description: Capture metadata: site or venue the footage was recorded at. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

station.description: Capture metadata: station or position within the site. `null` unless capture metadata was provided.

status.description: Lifecycle state. `in_progress` submissions are active attempts that have not submitted proof yet; `submitted` submissions await review; `approved` submissions were accepted and paid; `denied` submissions were rejected. `null` when the attempt ended without proof, taking it out of the public lifecycle — those attempts are absent from every public list and read.

submitted_at.description: When proof was submitted for review, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` while the attempt is in progress.

updated_at.description: When the submission was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

filename.description: Name the file was uploaded with.

url.description: Temporary download URL for the file.

ended_at.description: When the proof livestream ended, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` while it is still live — a feed with a `started_at` and no `ended_at` is streaming right now.

recording_url.description: Playback URL for a completed proof recording, when available.

started_at.description: When the proof livestream went live, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` before it starts.

thumbnail_url.description: Current proof thumbnail URL, when available.

title.description: Display title for the proof livestream.

filename_pattern.description: The naming convention for uploaded files, built from the required metadata fields.

manifest_schema_version.description: Schema version the client must stamp on the capture manifest it uploads.

min_clip_duration_seconds.description: Minimum length of a single clip, in seconds.

min_total_verified_duration_seconds.description: Total verified footage a submission must accumulate across all its clips before it can be submitted, in seconds. Always a whole number of hours.

items.description: Metadata fields a submission must provide, matching the `metadata` object on the submissions API.

single_continuous_take.description: Whether each clip must be one uninterrupted recording rather than stitched segments.

device_motion_units.description: Units for the device-motion channels, as a compact key=unit string.

min_rate_hz.description: Minimum sustained IMU sample rate in hertz for a clip to pass validation.

target_rate_hz.description: Target IMU sample rate in hertz.

warmup_min_rate_hz.description: Minimum IMU sample rate in hertz tolerated during the warmup window.

warmup_ns.description: Startup window, in nanoseconds, during which the relaxed warmup rate applies.

bitrate_ceiling_mbps.description: Maximum acceptable average bitrate, in megabits per second.

bitrate_floor_mbps.description: Minimum acceptable average bitrate, in megabits per second.

bitrate_target_mbps.description: Recommended average bitrate to encode at, in megabits per second.

camera_lens.description: Which physical lens to record with.

items.description: Accepted video codecs, in preference order.

embed_camera_metadata.description: Whether the client must also write the camera make and model into the video container's metadata. When `false`, the capture manifest and export CSV are the metadata carrier.

frame_gap_tolerance_ms.description: Longest stall between consecutive frames a clip may contain before the client rejects it, in milliseconds. Every frame is timestamped in the frame log, so a stall stays alignable downstream — this bounds how broken a capture may be, not how evenly it must be paced.

height.description: Required frame height in pixels — recorded footage must match exactly.

min_fov_degrees.description: Minimum acceptable horizontal field of view, in degrees.

preferred_fov_degrees.description: Preferred horizontal field of view, in degrees.

stabilization_mode.description: How the client must configure video stabilization: `off` disables EIS so raw motion is preserved for pose extraction, `on` requires it, `any` leaves the device default.

stabilization_required.description: Whether hardware/software stabilization must be enabled. True exactly when stabilization_mode is `on`.

width.description: Required frame width in pixels — recorded footage must match exactly.

card_id.description: The card this transaction was charged to, prefixed `icrd_`.

cardholder_id.description: The user the card is assigned to, prefixed `user_`. Null when the card has no assigned cardholder.

cashback_usd_amount.description: Cashback earned on this transaction as a USD amount. Zero for declined or ineligible transactions, and null when cashback has not been computed yet.

created_at.description: When the transaction was authorized, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code the merchant charged in.

declined_reason.description: Why the transaction was declined. Null unless `status` is `declined`.

international.description: True when the merchant is outside the card's home country.

local_amount.description: Amount the merchant charged in their own currency. Pair with `currency`.

merchant_category.description: Merchant category label, enriched where available and otherwise as the card network reported it.

merchant_icon_url.description: URL of the enriched merchant logo. Null when no logo was matched.

merchant_name.description: Merchant name, enriched where available and otherwise as the card network reported it.

posted_at.description: When the card network settled the transaction, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Null until it settles.

status.description: Current status of the transaction.

transaction_type.description: The kind of card transaction. Always `spend` today.

usd_amount.description: Amount charged in USD. Negative when the merchant refunded the card.

items.description: Payment methods this checkout withholds, even when the defaults would offer them.
Payment methods this checkout offers on top of whatever the defaults provide.

include_platform_defaults.description: Whether Whop's default set is the starting point. When `false`, only `enabled` is offered.

ConversionEvent.description: The pixel event optimized for. A standard event, or any custom pixel event name.

audience_size_lower_bound.description: Low end of the ad platform's estimate of how many people this option can reach. Null when the platform doesn't publish one.

audience_size_upper_bound.description: High end of the ad platform's estimate of how many people this option can reach. Null when the platform doesn't publish one.

behavior_type.description: What a behavior category is measured on, on ad platforms that scope them. Send it back on the `detailed_targeting.behaviors` entry alongside the id. Null for options that aren't scoped.

description.description: The ad platform's description of who the option covers, when it publishes one.
description.example: People who have expressed an interest in or like pages related to car washing and detailing.

id.description: The ad platform's ID for the option in its targeting taxonomy. Use it as the `id` of a `detailed_targeting` entry.

type.description: Which detailed-targeting field the option belongs in: `interests` and `behaviors` go in the matching `detailed_targeting` field; demographic categories (`life_events`, `industries`, `income`, `family_statuses`, `work_employers`, `work_positions`, `education_schools`, `education_majors`) go in `detailed_targeting.demographics` with this value as the entry's `type`.

account_id.description: The account the dispute was filed against, prefixed `biz_`.

amount.description: The disputed amount, in whole units of `currency`.

buyer.description: The customer who filed the dispute.

created_at.description: When the dispute was opened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code of the disputed amount.

evidence.description: The evidence packet sent to the processor to contest the dispute.

evidence_due_at.description: The deadline to submit evidence, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Whop reserves the last 24 hours before the processor's own cutoff to forward the submission.

evidence_editable.description: Whether `evidence` can still be changed and submitted.

evidence_locked_reason.description: Why evidence can no longer be edited. `null` while `evidence_editable` is true.

evidence_submitted_at.description: When the evidence was submitted to the processor, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

generated_response_attachment.description: The AI-generated representment document filed with the processor on the seller's behalf, once ready. Null until generation completes, and for disputes not using Whop Dispute Fighter.

inquiry.description: Whether this is a pre-dispute inquiry rather than a formal chargeback. Inquiries follow the same lifecycle but move no funds unless one escalates.

items.description: What the card issuer said when filing the dispute. Only populated when the issuer provides them, and listed in the order they were received.

plan_id.description: The plan the disputed payment was made on, prefixed `plan_`.

product_id.description: The product the disputed payment was for, prefixed `prod_`.

rapid_dispute_resolution.description: Whether Visa Rapid Dispute Resolution settled this automatically. These refund the customer without an evidence round.

reason.description: Why the customer says they are disputing, normalized across card networks. `other` covers a code Whop has not categorized yet — read `reason_code` for the raw value.

reason_code.description: The raw card-network or processor reason code, such as `10.4`.

status.description: Where the dispute stands. `needs_response` is awaiting evidence, `under_review` is with the processor, `won` returned the funds to the seller, `lost` returned them to the customer, and `closed` ended without a ruling. A dispute past its `evidence_due_at` reports `under_review` — the window to respond has closed.

updated_at.description: When the dispute was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

account_id.description: The account the alerted payment belongs to, prefixed `biz_`. `null` while the alert is unmatched.

actionable.description: Whether refunding the payment can still avoid a chargeback. `false` once the payment has been disputed or fully refunded, or when the alert could not be matched to a payment — `not_actionable_reason` says which.

amount.description: The alerted amount, in whole units of `currency`. This is what the issuer reported, which can differ from the payment's own amount.

card_brand.description: The card network as reported by the issuer, lowercased, such as `visa` or `mastercard`. `unknown` when the report carries neither a network nor a recognizable BIN.

created_at.description: When Whop received the alert, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code of the alerted amount.

fee_charged.description: Whether Whop charged the account an alert fee for this one. Always `false` for `early_fraud_warning`, which Whop is not billed for and never passes on.

issuer.description: Name of the bank that issued the card and filed the report.

not_actionable_reason.description: Why refunding can no longer avoid a chargeback. `network_resolved` when a Visa RDR already closed the case, `payment_unmatched` when no payment matched, `payment_not_captured` when it never captured money, `payment_disputed` once the payment carries a dispute, `payment_refunded` once fully refunded. `null` while `actionable` is true.

payment_id.description: The payment the issuer reported, prefixed `pay_`. `null` when Whop could not match the report to a payment.

product_id.description: The product the alerted payment was for, prefixed `prod_`.

reported_at.description: When the issuer filed the report, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Earlier than `created_at`, which is when Whop received it.

transaction_at.description: When the reported transaction was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

type.description: What the issuer sent. `early_fraud_warning` is a fraud report on a settled payment (Visa TC40 / Mastercard SAFE) — refunding still avoids the chargeback, and Whop never charges a fee for one. `dispute_alert` is a pre-dispute notice from the issuer's alert network, which Whop pays for and passes on as a fee. `rapid_dispute_resolution` is a Visa RDR case the network already closed by refunding the payment — nothing is left to act on.

updated_at.description: When the alert was last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

id.description: The attachment's ID. `null` for a Whop-hosted policy, which is not an uploaded file.

platform.description: Whether this is Whop's own hosted policy, standing in because the seller uploaded none. Sending it back on a PATCH changes nothing.

url.description: A URL to download the attachment.

email.description: The customer's email address. Requires the `member:email:read` scope; `null` without it.

member_id.description: The customer's member row on the account, prefixed `mem_`.

user_id.description: The customer's user ID, prefixed `user_`. `null` for a guest checkout.

access_activity_log.description: Log of the customer's access to the product, such as sign-in or download activity.
access_activity_log.example: Vehicle checked in 2026-01-04 09:02, released 2026-01-05 16:40. Signed release on file.

billing_address.description: The billing address the customer provided at checkout.

cancellation_policy_attachment.description: The cancellation policy document. Falls back to Whop's platform policy when the seller has not uploaded their own.

cancellation_policy_disclosure.description: How the cancellation policy was shown to the customer before purchase.
cancellation_policy_disclosure.example: Shown at checkout and again in the booking confirmation email.

customer_communication_attachment.description: Correspondence with the customer, or proof they used the product.

customer_email_address.description: The email address the customer used at checkout.

customer_name.description: The customer's name as given at checkout.

items.description: Additional evidence documents uploaded through `POST /disputes/{id}/upload_evidence`, beyond the four fixed slots. Each rides into the submitted packet under its `document_type`.

notes.description: Any additional context for the processor reviewing the dispute.
notes.example: Two-day ceramic coating completed and collected. Before and after photos attached.

product_description.description: What the customer purchased, in the seller's own words.
product_description.example: Two-stage paint correction with a three-year ceramic coating.

refund_policy_attachment.description: The refund policy document. Falls back to Whop's platform policy when the seller has not uploaded their own.

refund_policy_disclosure.description: How the refund policy was shown to the customer before purchase.
refund_policy_disclosure.example: Linked from the booking page and accepted at checkout.

refund_refusal_explanation.description: Why a refund was refused, when one was requested and denied.
refund_refusal_explanation.example: Work was completed and the vehicle collected, so the deposit is non-refundable.

service_date.description: When the product or service was delivered.

uncategorized_attachment.description: Supporting evidence that does not fit the other categories.

content_type.description: The uploaded file's MIME type. Uploads are restricted to the types the processor accepts.

created_at.description: When the file was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

document_type.description: What kind of evidence the document is.

filename.description: The original filename, including its extension.

multipart_chunk_size.description: The byte size each part (except the last) must be. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

multipart_upload_id.description: The ID of the multipart upload, passed back to `complete`. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

items.description: The presigned URL for each part. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

object.description: The type of this object, always `file`.

size.description: The file size in bytes. `null` until the upload has finished.

upload_headers.description: Headers to send with the upload PUT. Present only on create.

upload_status.description: Where the file is in its upload lifecycle.

upload_url.description: Presigned URL to PUT the file's bytes to. Present only on create, and only for single-part uploads.

url.description: A URL to download the file: a permanent CDN URL for public files, a signed expiring URL for private ones. `null` until the upload has finished.

visibility.description: `public` files are served via an unsigned CDN URL; `private` files via a signed, expiring URL.

received_at.description: When the comment was received, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

text.description: What the issuer wrote, as received.
text.example:
Note: Cardholder states the ceramic coating appointment never took place
Cancellation method: By phone

amount.description: What the customer was charged, in whole units of the payment's currency.

card_brand.description: Card brand, when the customer paid by card.

card_last4.description: Last four digits of the card, when the customer paid by card.

created_at.description: When the payment was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code of the payment. Can differ from the dispute's currency when the processor settles in another currency.

payment_instrument.description: The instrument this payment was made with, shaped for display: the method type, a buyer-facing name, the standard icon set, and the card facts when it was a card. Null when the payment names no method.

payment_method_type.description: How the customer paid, such as `card` or `paypal`.

payment_processor.description: The processor that handled the payment, such as `stripe`.

level.description: What the user is notified about in the experience: `all` notifications, only `mentions`, or `nothing`.

scope.description: What the preference applies to. Echo it back to `PATCH /users/me/preferences/notifications` to change this preference.

created_at.description: When the export was requested, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

download_url.description: A short-lived link to download the finished CSV. `null` until `status` is `completed`, and again once the export has expired.

expires_at.description: When the CSV is deleted and the export moves to `expired`, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Exports are retained for 30 days.

resource.description: The resource that was exported, e.g. `receipts`, `members`, or `payouts`.

status.description: `pending` or `processing` while the CSV is generated, `completed` when the download is ready, `failed` if it errored, `expired` once the CSV has been deleted.

updated_at.description: When the export last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

created_at.description: When the file was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

filename.description: The original filename, including its extension.

multipart_chunk_size.description: The byte size each part (except the last) must be. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

multipart_upload_id.description: The ID of the multipart upload, passed back to `complete`. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

items.description: The presigned URL for each part. Present only on create, and only for multipart uploads.

object.description: The type of this object, always `file`.

size.description: The file size in bytes. `null` until the upload has finished.

upload_headers.description: Headers to send with the upload PUT. Present only on create.

upload_status.description: Where the file is in its upload lifecycle.

upload_url.description: Presigned URL to PUT the file's bytes to. Present only on create, and only for single-part uploads.

url.description: A URL to download the file: a permanent CDN URL for public files, a signed expiring URL for private ones. `null` until the upload has finished.

visibility.description: `public` files are served via an unsigned CDN URL; `private` files via a signed, expiring URL.

part_number.description: The 1-based index of this part within the multipart upload.

url.description: The presigned URL to PUT this part's bytes to.

code.description: ISO 639 code the ad-group `languages` field takes, such as `en`.

type.description: Always `languages`. The option goes in the ad-group `languages` field.

account.description: The viewer account that owns this row's ledger. Present only when the response aggregates owned accounts (include_owned_accounts=true); omitted otherwise.

amount.description: Signed amount in the currency's smallest precision units.

available_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp these funds became (or are scheduled to become) withdrawable: the posted time for already-settled funds, or 00:00:00 UTC on the scheduled release date for pending funds. Present only on inflows entering the balance (payments, top-ups, incoming transfers/affiliate); null on payouts, refunds, disputes and on-chain rows. The available_after/before filters window on its UTC settlement date.

currency.description: Currency for this ledger activity.

code.description: Currency code.

precision.description: Precision factor for the currency, for example `100000000` for USD.

ledger_account_id.description: The ledger account (a ldgr_ identifier) this row belongs to. Present only when the response aggregates owned accounts (include_owned_accounts=true); omitted otherwise. Pair it with `account` to scope drawers and dashboard links to the owning business.

line_type.description: The ledger line category this activity was posted under.

payment.description: Payment related to this ledger activity. Included when rich resource hydration is enabled and the movement is tied to a payment.

amount.description: Total charged by the payment.

card_brand.description: Card brand, when the customer paid by card.

card_last4.description: Last four digits of the card, when the customer paid by card.

created_at.description: When the payment was created.

payment_method_type.description: How the customer paid, such as `card` or `paypal`.

payment_processor.description: Processor that handled the payment, such as `stripe`.

plan.description: Plan associated with the payment, when applicable.

product.description: Product associated with the payment, when applicable.

user.description: Customer associated with the payment. Email requires member:email:read.

email.description: Customer email, or null without member:email:read.

payment_id.description: Payment ID for any payment-related activity, including refunds and disputes.

plan_id.description: ID of the plan associated with the payment, when applicable.

plan_name.description: Name of the plan associated with the payment, when applicable.

posted_at.description: When the activity posted to the ledger.

product_id.description: ID of the product associated with the payment, when applicable.

product_name.description: Name of the product associated with the payment, when applicable.

resource.description: Resource associated with this ledger activity.

status.description: Bounty lifecycle status.

last4.description: Last four digits of the bank account.
Last four digits of the card.

email_identifier.description: Email identifier for email-based payment methods.

authorized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the transaction was authorized.

card_id.description: Identifier of the card that the transaction was charged to.

cashback_usd.description: Cashback earned on this transaction as a USD decimal string. Zero for declined or ineligible transactions; null when cashback has not been computed yet.

declined_reason.description: Reason the transaction was declined (when status is declined).

local_amount.description: Amount the merchant charged in their local currency, as a decimal string. Pair with local_currency.

local_currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the merchant-charged amount in local_amount.

posted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the transaction was settled by the card network.

status.description: Current card transaction status.

usd_amount.description: The processor-settled USD amount as a decimal string. The ledger's USDT leg is posted 1:1 from this value.

amount_float.description: Payout amount as a decimal number in the destination currency (payout sources only; requires payout:withdrawal:read).

card_brand.description: Card brand used by the payment source.

chain.description: Chain the deposit landed on, for example plasma (onchain_transaction sources only).

claim_url.description: Public claim URL for the airdrop link (airdrop_link sources only).

created_at.description: Payout creation time as an ISO 8601 timestamp (payout sources only; requires payout:withdrawal:read).

estimated_arrival.description: Estimated arrival as an ISO 8601 timestamp (payout sources only; requires payout:withdrawal:read).

from_amount.description: Amount converted out of from_currency as a decimal string (swap sources only).

from_currency.description: Lowercase currency code converted from (swap sources only).

payer_name.description: Name of the entity processing the payout (payout sources only; requires payout:withdrawal:read).

payment_amount.description: Total charged by the payment source.

payment_method_type.description: Payment method used by the payment source.

payment_processor.description: Processor used by the payment source.

payout_destination.description: Payout destination display info (payout sources only).

payout_token_nickname.description: Saved payout destination nickname (payout sources only).

reason.description: Why the activity happened. On transfer sources this is the transfer reason, for example pool_top_up or bounty_return. On payout sources it explains why the payout was canceled, denied, or failed (requires payout:withdrawal:read); null while the payout is progressing normally.

risk_review_hold.description: Whether this payout is currently held for manual risk review (payout sources only; requires payout:withdrawal:read).

sender_address.description: Sender wallet address or onramp provider identifier (onchain_transaction sources only).

status.description: Lifecycle status. On payout sources this is the payout status (requires payout:withdrawal:read); on airdrop_link sources it is the claim-link status (ungated); on payment and top-up sources it is the friendly payment status such as succeeded/pending/failed (ungated).

to_amount.description: Amount received in to_currency as a decimal string (swap sources only).

to_currency.description: Lowercase currency code converted to (swap sources only).

tx_hash.description: On-chain transaction hash (onchain_transaction and swap sources only).

user_email.description: Email of the customer associated with the payment. Requires member:email:read.

user_id.description: ID of the customer associated with the payment.

user_name.description: Display name of the customer associated with the payment.

code.description: The standardized code the ad-group `regions` field takes: an ISO 3166-1 code for countries (`US`) or an ISO 3166-2 code for states and provinces (`US-CA`, `CA-ON`). Null for a location that has no standard code, such as a city or a metro area — target those by `key` in the `regions` cities list instead.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 code of the country the location sits in.

country_name.description: Name of the country the location sits in.

key.description: The ad platform's key for the location in its location taxonomy. Use it as the `key` of a `regions` city or zip entry.

location_type.description: Granularity of the location. Which of these an ad platform reports depends on how finely it divides its location taxonomy.

region.description: Name of the state or province a city sits in. Null for everything but cities.

type.description: Always `locations`. The option goes in the ad-group `regions` field.

amount_charged.description: USD amount charged to the account's balance for this generation. `null` if the generation wasn't billed.

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the asset reached a terminal state. `null` while `processing`.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the generation was requested.

currency.description: Currency of `amount_charged`. Always `usd`.

error_message.description: Why generation failed. `null` unless status is `failed`.
error_message.example: The generation provider rejected the prompt. The charge was refunded.

file.description: The produced file, usable anywhere attachments are accepted. `null` until the asset is `ready`.

generation.description: The inputs the asset was generated from.

media_type.description: The kind of media this asset holds.

source.description: How the asset was created. Always `generated`.

status.description: Lifecycle state: `processing` while generation runs, `ready` when the file is available, `failed` when generation failed and the charge was refunded.

url.description: CDN URL for downloading the file.

duration_seconds.description: Requested video length in seconds. `null` for images.

prompt.description: What the asset was generated from.
prompt.example: A 9:16 product showcase of a cordless power scrubber

items.description: Reference image file IDs (`file_` prefixed) supplied at generation time.

resolution.description: Requested video resolution. `null` for images. `1080p` is not supported by Seedance 2.0 Fast or Mini; `4k` is only supported by Seedance 2.0.

access_level.description: What the member can reach on the account: `customer` for paying members, `admin` for team members, `no_access` once every grant has lapsed.

account_id.description: The account this member belongs to, prefixed `biz_`.

created_at.description: When the member record was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

joined_at.description: When the member first joined the account, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

last_accessed_at.description: When the member last opened the account's content, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` if they never have.

status.description: `joined` while the member is part of the account, `left` after they leave.

user.description: The user behind this member. `null` when the buyer is another business rather than a person.

account.description: The account (seller) this membership belongs to.

cancel_at_period_end.description: Whether the membership is set to cancel when the current billing period ends. Only meaningful for recurring plans.

created_at.description: When the membership was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

current_period_end.description: When the current billing period renews, or when a non-renewing membership expires, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` for one-time purchases with no expiration.

license_key.description: The software license key for this membership. Only present when the product includes a software licensing experience.

member.description: The caller's member row on the account. Present only when the membership belongs to the caller; `null` on seller-side reads.

metadata.description: Custom key-value pairs stored on the membership, commonly used for software licensing.

plan_id.description: The plan the buyer purchased, prefixed `plan_`.

product_id.description: The product this membership grants access to, prefixed `prod_`.

status.description: Billing state of the membership. `active`/`trialing` memberships grant access; `past_due` is the grace period after a failed payment; `completed` one-time purchases keep access; `canceled`/`expired` do not.

user_id.description: The buyer, prefixed `user_`. `null` when the buyer is another business or the membership is unclaimed.

route.description: Account public route identifier — the `whop.com/{route}` storefront path.

access_level.description: What the member can reach on the account: `customer` for paying members, `admin` for team members, `no_access` once every grant has lapsed.

last_accessed_at.description: When the member last opened the account's content, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` if they never have.

position.description: The member's sort position in the buyer's own account list. `null` until they arrange it.

amount.description: The amount in major units, as an exact decimal string — `"10.00"` is ten dollars. A string so no float rounds it in transit.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, lowercase.

decimals.description: How many decimal places the amount CARRIES — the precision the charge itself runs at.

display_decimals.description: How many decimal places to SHOW. Usually equal to `decimals`, and deliberately not always: COP is charged in centavos but written in whole pesos, so it is `2` and `0`. Format the number in your own locale using this.

account.description: Account the notification belongs to. `null` when the notification is not associated with an account.

attachment_url.description: Image displayed alongside the notification — the sender's avatar, or the default notification image.

content.description: The body text of the notification displayed to the user.

created_at.description: When the notification was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

experience.description: Experience the notification is related to. `null` when not tied to a specific experience.

id.description: Notification ID. Feed rows carry a composite id that doubles as the list cursor.

iframe_link.description: The same destination on the app's own domain, which the Whop web and mobile clients embed instead of navigating to it. Only relevant if you render Whop apps yourself. `null` when the notification carries its own `link`.

link.description: The whop.com page the notification opens, as a normal top-level navigation. This is the link to use unless you host Whop apps yourself. `null` when the notification has no click-through destination.

mentions_me.description: Whether the authenticated user was directly mentioned in this notification.

rest_path.description: Additional path information appended to the notification's deep link, if any.

sender.description: User who triggered the notification. `null` when it was system-generated.

subject.description: The title line of the notification displayed to the user.

topic.description: Topic category the notification belongs to, used for grouping and preference management. `null` when uncategorized.

logo_url.description: Account logo image URL. `null` when the account has not uploaded one.

route.description: URL slug of the account's store page on whop.com.

account_id.description: Account the experience belongs to, prefixed `biz_`.

has_unread.description: Whether the caller has unread notifications in this experience.

important_count.description: Number of unread important (mention) notifications in this experience.

last_viewed_at.description: When the caller last viewed the experience, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. `null` when never viewed.

icon_url.description: Icon image URL. Always present — the default app icon when none is uploaded.

account_id.description: Account the preference is scoped to (member notifications), prefixed `biz_`.

channel.description: Delivery channel the preference applies to. `null` applies to every channel.

experience_id.description: Experience the preference is scoped to, prefixed `exp_`.

team_account_id.description: Account whose team notifications the preference is scoped to, prefixed `biz_`.

topic_id.description: Notification topic the preference is scoped to, prefixed `topic_`.

level.description: What the user is now notified about in this scope, or `null` if the preference was cleared and the scope inherits its default again.

object.description: Which kind of preference was written: `experience_notification_preference` for an experience level, `notification_preference` for a topic override.

scope.description: The scope that was written, resolved. `null` on a dimension means the preference is not narrowed there.

default_preference_value.description: Whether notifications for this topic are enabled by default when the user has not set a preference.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of what notifications in this topic are about. `null` when no description has been set.
description.example: A customer books and pays for a detail

id.description: Notification topic ID, prefixed `topic_`. This is the value the notification preference endpoints take as `topic_id`.

identifier.description: Stable, human-readable name for the category, such as `new-follower`. Unlike `id`, it is the same in every environment, which makes it the value to match on in code and to read in logs. Treat it as an opaque string: the set is open and the casing is historical rather than normalized.

is_mention.description: Whether this topic exclusively handles mention-based notifications.

name.description: Display name shown in notification preference settings.

topic_type.description: Scope of the topic: whether it applies to an account, a user, or an account's team.

default_preference_value.description: Whether notifications for this topic are enabled by default when the user has not set a preference.

is_mention.description: Whether this topic exclusively handles mention-based notifications.

topic_type.description: Scope of the topic: whether it applies to an account, a user, or an account's team.

account_id.description: The account the grant is scoped to, prefixed `biz_`. `null` when the user authorized the app for themselves rather than for one of their accounts.

app_id.description: The app this grant authorizes, prefixed `app_`.

authorized_at.description: When the user last authorized the app, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

created_at.description: When the user first authorized the app, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

redirect_url.description: Where to send the user to finish the flow: the `redirect_uri` you supplied with the authorization `code` appended, and `state` when you supplied one. Its scheme, host, port, and path come back exactly as sent — never re-cased or re-encoded — because the client matches them against its registered URI. Returned only once, on create: the code is single-use and expires 10 minutes after it is issued, so redirect immediately.

revoked_at.description: When the grant was revoked, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` while it is still in force. A revoked grant authorizes nothing — treat its `scopes` as no longer granted.

items.description: Every permission the user has granted this app, accumulated across authorizations, for example `member:basic:read`. `GET /api_keys/permissions` names and describes each one.

created_at.description: When the user registered this passkey, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

credential_id.description: The WebAuthn credential ID as a base64url string. Pass it in `allowCredentials` when you run a ceremony against this specific passkey.

id.description: Passkey ID, prefixed `wcred_`. Use it to delete the passkey.

last_used_at.description: When this passkey last completed a WebAuthn ceremony, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` if it never has.

nickname.description: The name the user gave this passkey, usually the device it lives on.

account_number.description: The account to send to, in the local scheme's format — `account_number_label` says what to call it.

account_number_label.description: What to call `account_number` when showing it, in the local scheme's own terms — `CLABE` in Mexico, for example.

amount.description: Exactly what the buyer must send, in the charged currency.

bank_account_type.description: The kind of account receiving the transfer, such as a checking account, in the local system's own vocabulary.

bank_branch.description: The receiving branch, where the local system routes by branch.

bank_code.description: The receiving bank's code in the local clearing system.

beneficiary_document.description: The account holder's tax or identity document number, where the local system needs it to send.

beneficiary_document_type.description: What kind of document `beneficiary_document` is, in the local system's own vocabulary.

beneficiary_name.description: Who the account belongs to — the name the buyer's bank may ask them to confirm.

document_url.description: A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.

expires_at.description: When these details stop being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

instructions.description: The rail's own step-by-step payment text, when it supplies one.
instructions.example: Send the exact amount from your own bank account and include the reference SHINE-8237 so the transfer can be matched to your order.

reference.description: The reference the buyer must attach to the transfer so it can be matched to this payment.

routing_number.description: The receiving bank's routing number for US transfers.

secondary_account_number.description: A second account number, where the rail publishes the same destination in more than one format.

secondary_account_number_label.description: What to call `secondary_account_number` when showing it.

kind.description: Always `bank_transfer`: account details the buyer sends money to from their own bank.

PaymentInstructions.description: What to show the buyer so they can pay. `kind` picks the shape and the details sit under the key named for it, so switching on `kind` gives you exactly that kind's payload. Every detail field is optional — the rails behind these methods publish them unevenly — but a kind that arrives with `document_url` can always fall back to sending the buyer to that hosted copy of the instructions.

card.description: Card payments only: the card's network and last four.

display_name.description: Buyer-facing instrument name — "Visa •••• 4242" when the card surfaced, else the method's own name ("Klarna").

icons.description: The standard icon set: square and card shapes, each in light and dark colorways.

installment_count.description: Installment methods only: how many payments the charge splits into. Data, not copy — compose and translate the label client-side.

payment_method_type.description: The payment method type identifier, e.g. `card`, `klarna`, `apple_pay`.

brand.description: The network identifier (`visa`, `amex`, …), matching `card.networks` entries and saved card payment methods.

last4.description: The card's last four digits, when captured.

code.description: A machine-readable classification of the failure.

decline_code.description: The reason the payment was declined.

message.description: A human-readable explanation of the failure.

account_id.description: ID of the account the domain is registered for, prefixed `biz_`.

created_at.description: When the domain was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

hostname.description: Hostname the checkout is served from (e.g. `checkout.example.com`).

provider.description: Wallet provider the domain is registered with.

status.description: Verification status. `pending` means the provider could not fetch the domain-association file yet; only `verified` domains show wallet payment methods at checkout.

updated_at.description: When the domain was last updated, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

png_1x.description: Raster fallback at the shape's native size.

svg.description: The vector file. Prefer this everywhere SVG renders.

PaymentNextAction.description: What the buyer must do to finish. `type` picks the shape and each type carries only its own `data`, so switching on `type` gives you exactly that step's payload.

data.description: How long the wait can last.

items.description: Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.

type.description: Always `await_confirmation`: nothing to show — the buyer has done their part and the rail settles out of band. Poll `status` until it moves.

expires_at.description: When the confirmation window closes, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. A payment still unconfirmed by then will not succeed — watch `status` for the failed attempt.

data.description: The instructions. `kind` picks the shape, and the details sit under the key named for it: `voucher`, `qr`, or `bank_transfer`.

items.description: Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.

type.description: Always `display_instructions`: show the buyer `data` — what to pay, where, and by when. The payment completes once they pay and the rail confirms it, so keep polling `status`.

items.description: Where this step can be presented: `inline` inside your own page, `full_page` as a top-level navigation. Pick whichever listed mode suits your surface.

type.description: Always `redirect`: send the buyer to `data.url`. The provider hands them back to `return_url` when they are done.

frame_max_width.description: The widest the provider's page lays out usefully, in CSS pixels — cap a frame or dialog presenting it at this width. `null` when the page fills whatever width it is given.

url.description: The provider's page for this payment, as an absolute URL — take the buyer there.

expected_by.description: When the payment is expected to settle, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

amount.description: Exactly what the buyer must pay, in the charged currency.

document_url.description: A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.

expires_at.description: When the code stops being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

key.description: An account key the buyer can pay to directly (Colombia's Bre-B llave), for apps that take a key instead of a scan.

qr_code.description: The QR code's contents, ready to render as a scannable image — `qr_format` says how it is encoded.

kind.description: Always `qr`: a code the buyer scans with their banking app.

id.description: The payment this status describes, prefixed `pay_`.

last_payment_error.description: Details of the most recent failed attempt, or `null` when the payment has not failed.

next_action.description: What the buyer must do next while `status` is `requires_action`, otherwise `null`. `type` picks the shape and each variant carries only its own `data`, so switching on `type` gives you exactly that step's payload.

processing_details.description: Present while `status` is `processing` on a settlement rail, otherwise `null`.

return_url.description: Where to send the buyer once the payment reaches a resting state, or `null` to leave them where they are. Editable until they return — see the return_url operation.

status.description: How far the payment has got. `requires_confirmation` — nothing attempted yet, or the last attempt failed and can be retried. `requires_action` — the buyer has a step outstanding; see `next_action`. `confirming` — the buyer has done their part and the processor is deciding. `processing` — the money is moving; see `processing_details`. `succeeded` — collected. `canceled` — voided or written off.

amount.description: Exactly what the buyer must pay, in the charged currency.

barcode.description: The barcode's contents, when the voucher carries one — render it in the symbology named by `barcode_format`.

barcode_format.description: The symbology `barcode` is encoded in, such as `CODE_128`.

company_name.description: Who the payment is made out to.

document_url.description: A hosted page with the complete, printable instructions. If you would rather not render the details yourself, send the buyer here.

expires_at.description: When the voucher stops being payable, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

provider_name.description: The network the buyer pays at, such as OXXO.

reference.description: The voucher's number — what the buyer reads out or types at the counter to pay.

kind.description: Always `voucher`: a code the buyer pays in person, at a convenience store or bank counter.

action.description: The permission action's identifier, for example `company:basic:read`.

allowed_on_api_key.description: Whether an API key can be granted the permission.

allowed_on_app.description: Whether an app can request and be granted the permission.

allowed_on_user.description: Whether the permission can be granted to user tokens.

category.description: The category the action is grouped under, or `null` when uncategorized.

description.description: What granting the action allows.
description.example: Download the account's product list as a CSV.

items.description: System roles that include the permission.

PermissionAction.description: A permission action identifier, such as `company:basic:read`.

firing_data_ok.description: False when the event lookup failed, meaning `host_events` and `last_seen_days` are incomplete.

items.description: Conversion event names detected on the requested page or fired recently anywhere on its hostname or final redirect hostname.

installed.description: Whether the pixel was seen. Without a `url` this answers for the whole account: true when it has sent events recently. With a `url` it answers for THAT page only — true when the page is hosted on Whop, when the page itself has sent events recently, or when the pixel was found in its source. Events the account sent from other pages do not make a given `url` installed.

last_fired_days.description: Event name to whole days since that event last fired, e.g. `{ "lead": 3 }`. Carries events that fired too long ago to count as installed, so you can prompt to re-check rather than report them missing.

last_seen_days.description: Days since the pixel last sent an event, within a 30-day window. `null` when it hasn't sent one in that window — which includes a pixel installed moments ago.

native_tracking.description: True when `url` is hosted on Whop, so no pixel snippet is required.

items.description: Conversion event names detected on the requested page, from its recent events or its source and linked scripts.

reachable.description: Whether the page could be loaded. `null` when the request included no URL, and `true` when events settled the answer without a fetch.

url.description: The URL that was checked, after normalization. `null` when the request didn't include one.

cancel_discount_intervals.description: Billing intervals the cancellation discount applies to (`0` forever, `1` first payment, or a month count). `null` when none is offered or the actor lacks the `plan:basic:read` scope.

amount.description: The amount in question, in whole units of `currency`.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code of the amount.

escalated.description: Whether Whop is involved — either reviewing the case, or waiting on the side named by `status` for something it asked for while reviewing.

outcome.description: Who prevailed on the claim. `null` until the case closes. Read `refund` for whether any money actually moved.

payment.description: The payment the case was opened against.

plan_id.description: The plan the payment was made on, prefixed `plan_`.

product_id.description: The product the payment was for, prefixed `prod_`.

reason.description: What the customer says went wrong. Shares the `/disputes` vocabulary, so a case that later becomes a chargeback reports the same complaint.

response_due_at.description: When the next response is due, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

status.description: Who the case is waiting on. `awaiting_merchant` and `awaiting_customer` name the side that owes a response, `under_review` means Whop is deciding, and `closed` means it is settled — read `outcome` for how.

code.description: A machine-readable classification of the failure, e.g. `enrollment_declined`. Absent when the buyer simply abandoned the setup.

id.description: The setup this status describes, prefixed `sint_`.

last_setup_error.description: Why the setup ended where it did, or `null` when nothing has failed. Present on `canceled` — a buyer who abandoned carries no code, one refused by the provider does.

next_action.description: What the buyer must do next while `status` is `requires_action`, otherwise `null`. `type` picks the shape and each variant carries only its own `data`, so switching on `type` gives you exactly that step's payload.

return_url.description: Where to send the buyer once the setup reaches a resting state, or `null` to leave them where they are.

status.description: How far the setup has got. **A 200 means we answered, not that the method was saved — always branch on this.** `requires_action` — the buyer has a step outstanding; see `next_action`. `processing` — the buyer has done their part and the processor is deciding. `succeeded` — the payment method is saved, and only this one means saved. `canceled` — abandoned or refused; see `last_setup_error` to tell which.

items.description: Ways this post can't be used on an ad. `lead_form_ineligible`: post can't be used in lead form ads. `promotion_ineligible`: the platform won't promote this post at all — always present when that's true, alongside a reason code when one is identified. `copyrighted_music`: post uses music the platform does not allow for ads. `messenger_destination`, `instagram_destination`, `whatsapp_destination`: the post's own button opens that chat app, so the post can only run in an ad group that sends people to the same one — always accompanied by `lead_form_ineligible`. thumbnail_url.description: Poster image for video posts (always set for TikTok, which is video-only); null for image posts, where media_url is already the image.

banner.description: The user's profile banner wrapper. `null` when the user has no banner.

bio.example: Ceramic coating specialist. Detailing cars in Austin since 2016.

earnings_usd.description: The user's gross USD income over time. Populated only on single-user self reads for callers with balance-read scope; `null` otherwise.

verification.description: Identity verification status for the user's `individual` (KYC) and `business` (KYB) profiles. Each is `null` until created, otherwise a `status` of `not_started`, `pending`, `approved`, or `rejected`.

api_version_date.description: The dated API version (Api-Version-Date) that v1 payloads for this endpoint are pinned to: events serialize exactly like a REST read at this version (the native serializer where the resource has one). child_resource_events.description: Whether events are sent for child resources. For example, if the webhook is on an account, enabling this sends events only from its connected accounts.

items.description: Event types this webhook is subscribed to, in dot form (for example `payment.succeeded`).

resource_id.description: ID of the resource (account or app) this webhook is attached to.

items.description: The subset of subscribed event types that support sending test payloads, in dot form.

url.description: Destination URL where webhook payloads are delivered via HTTP POST.
